constitucion.title: Constitución Política de la República de Costa Rica de 7 de noviembre de 1949 (y sus reformas)
constitucion.note: The TSE's consolidated text. Art. 105 (referendum, as reformed by Law 8281 of 2002), 106 (57 deputies elected by provinces, as reformed by Law 2741 of 1961), 107 (four-year term), 133 (first Sunday of February), 138 (40 percent threshold, runoff on the first Sunday of April), 168 (provinces, cantons and districts; plebiscite before a new province), 169 and 171 (municipal government and regidores for four years), 172 (a síndico for each district; concejos municipales de distrito, as reformed by Law 8105 of 2001), 100 and 158 (magistrates appointed by the Supreme Court and elected by the Assembly).

codigo_electoral.title: Código Electoral, Ley n.° 8765 (y sus reformas)
codigo_electoral.note: Art. 12(p) (the TSE organizes the referendums and plebiscites of Constitution arts. 105 and 168), 52(k) (parties choose their candidates; a party convention's presidential nominee is final), 147 (partial extraordinary elections for a municipality that disintegrates or under Código Municipal art. 19), 150 (national elections on the first Sunday of February; municipal elections on the first Sunday of February two years later; every four years), 201-205 (majority for president, cociente and subcociente for deputies, regidores and district councils, relative majority for mayors, intendentes and síndicos).

codigo_municipal.title: Código Municipal, Ley n.° 7794 (y sus reformas)
codigo_municipal.note: Art. 13(g) (the municipal council appoints the juntas de educación and juntas administrativas), 13(k) (the council calls plebiscites, referendos and cabildos, with TSE delegates attending), 14 (mayor and two vice-mayors), 19 (plebiscite to remove the mayor, two thirds of votes cast and at least 10 percent of the canton's electors), 21 (regidores by population), 54-55 (district councils).

estadisticas.title: Estadísticas de elecciones
estadisticas.note: The TSE's statistics page: Cómputo de votos workbooks (xlsx in zip) and books (pdf) for every election from February 2002 to February 2026 (national 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, 2026; municipal December 2002, December 2006, December 2010, February 2016, 2020, 2024; referendum 2007); Estadísticas del sufragio (turnout by sex, age and zone) from 1994; Elecciones en cifras 1953-2022; Municipales en cifras 2002-2024. declaratorias.title: Declaratorias definitivas de elecciones
declaratorias.note: The TSE's index of its definitive declarations of election, 1998-2026: president, deputies, regidores (and síndicos in 1998), mayors, district councils, intendencias and concejos municipales de distrito, the 2007 referendum (resolution 2944-E-2007, 7 October 2007) and the April 2019 plebiscite on the seat of Río Cuarto canton (resolution 2688-E11-2019).

cifras.title: Elecciones en cifras 1953-2022
cifras.note: TSE Unidad de Estadística, November 2022. Cuadro 1.1 lists the 18 presidential elections 1953-2022 with electorate and votes; Parte III gives each presidential election's votes by party and province, first and second rounds. Presidential only; no deputies or municipal results.

muni_cifras.title: Municipales en cifras 2002-2024
muni_cifras.note: TSE Unidad de Estadística, February 2025. Cuadro 1 gives the six municipal elections 2002-2024; Cuadro 8 counts the posts elected in each by office (regidurías, sindicaturas, alcaldías, concejalías de distrito, concejalías municipales de distrito, intendencias); note 1/ says regidores were elected with the general elections in 2002, 2006 and 2010. Parte III gives mayoral votes by party for each canton.

computo2024.title: Cómputo de votos y declaratorias de elección, elecciones municipales 4 de febrero de 2024
computo2024.note: Includes decree 6-2023 convening the election: art. 2, a mayoralty in each of the 84 municipalities; art. 3, regidores per canton; art. 4, a síndico in 491 districts of the Administrative Territorial Division (all but uninhabited Isla del Coco), concejos municipales de distrito with an intendencia in the seven districts of Cervantes, Cóbano, Colorado, Lepanto, Paquera, Peñas Blancas and Tucurrique, and district councils in the rest. classes.name: Presidencia y Vicepresidencias de la República
classes.finest_note: Votes by voting center (or electoral district) in the Cómputo de votos workbooks from 2002, abroad by country from 2014; by province only for 1953-1998 (Elecciones en cifras). The 2026 book mentions an interactive report by junta receptora.
classes.note: One ticket of a president and two vice presidents, elected nationally with more than 40 percent of valid votes, else a runoff between the top two on the first Sunday of April (Constitution art. 138); four-year term, no immediate re-election. Runoffs were held in 2002, 2014, 2018 and 2022. Elections before the 1949 Constitution are the abolished class presidente_1949.

cadence.runoff_rule: If no ticket exceeds 40 percent of valid votes, the top two meet on the first Sunday of April (Constitution art. 138).
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vice president succeeds; there is no special election (Constitution art. 135).

classes.name: Diputaciones a la Asamblea Legislativa
classes.finest_note: Votes by voting center (or electoral district) in the Cómputo de votos workbooks from 2002; the 1998 declaration gives provinces; no official digital results for 1953-1994
classes.note: Unicameral, elected on the presidential ballot day by closed lists in the seven provinces, seats allotted by population, by cociente and subcociente (Hare quota, largest remainders, with a threshold of half a quota; Código Electoral arts. 201-205); 45 deputies in 1953 and 1958, 57 since Law 2741 of 1961 (Constitution art. 106); four-year term, no immediate re-election (art. 107). Votes from abroad count only for president.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Filled by the next candidate on the party's provincial list, declared by the TSE (Código Electoral art. 207); no by-elections.

classes.finest_note: Votes by electoral district in the 2007 Cómputo de votos workbooks
classes.note: A referendum approves or repeals a law or partial constitutional reform when called by 5 percent of registered electors, two thirds of the Assembly, or the Executive with an absolute majority of the Assembly (Constitution art. 105, added by Law 8281 of 2002, in force 20 June 2002; Law 8492 of 2006). The only one held approved the Central America-Dominican Republic free trade agreement on 7 October 2007.

classes.name: Plebiscitos territoriales
classes.name_en: Territorial plebiscites run by the TSE
classes.note: The TSE runs the plebiscite that must approve a new province in the provinces losing territory (Constitution art. 168; Código Electoral art. 12(p)) and plebiscites ordered by law on cantonal matters, such as the April 2019 vote on the seat (cabecera) of the new canton of Río Cuarto. No province has been created since 1949. Earlier boundary plebiscites have not been found in the TSE's published declarations.

classes.name: Asamblea Nacional Constituyente
classes.note: The Asamblea Nacional Constituyente that wrote the 1949 Constitution was elected on 8 December 1948, before the TSE existed. A future constituent assembly would be elected by cociente and subcociente on the national total (Código Electoral arts. 150, 201 and 204; Constitution art. 196).
classes.disposition_reason: The TSE publishes no results for the 1948 election, which an earlier electoral tribunal ran; none has been held since.

classes.name: Elecciones de Presidente y Congreso antes de 1949
classes.name_en: Presidential and congressional elections before the 1949 Constitution
classes.note: Heads of state and presidents, and the Congreso Constitucional, from the 1820s to 1948: indirect (through electoral assemblies) until 1913, direct afterwards, declared by Congress. The 1948 election was annulled and the Congreso dissolved; a junta governed until the 1949 Constitution.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes these results; the TSE's series begins in 1953, and the Asamblea Legislativa's site refuses automated requests.

classes.name: Convenciones y asambleas de los partidos
classes.note: Parties choose their candidates under their own statutes, through district, cantonal, provincial and national assemblies or, for president, open conventions such as Liberación Nacional's; the convention's presidential nominee is final (Código Electoral art. 52(k)).
classes.disposition_reason: Run, counted and published by the parties themselves; the TSE neither administers nor publishes them.

classes.name: Magistraturas de la Corte Suprema y del TSE
classes.name_en: Supreme Court and electoral tribunal magistrates
classes.note: Supreme Court magistrates are elected by two thirds of the Legislative Assembly for eight years (Constitution art. 158); TSE magistrates are appointed by two thirds of the Supreme Court (art. 100). No judge is elected by voters.
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect votes of the Assembly and the Court, not popular elections.

classes.name: Elecciones de colegios profesionales, cooperativas, sindicatos, universidades y asociaciones
classes.name_en: Professional bodies, cooperatives, unions, universities and associations
classes.note: Professional colleges, cooperatives, unions, public universities, community development associations (including those governing indigenous territories) and water associations elect their own boards under their own laws and statutes.
classes.disposition_reason: Internal votes of private or corporate bodies, not run by the TSE.

classes.name: Juntas de educación y juntas administrativas
classes.note: The boards of public schools (juntas de educación) and secondary schools (juntas administrativas) are appointed by the municipal council (Código Municipal art. 13(g)). Costa Rica has no elected special-purpose districts.
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the municipal council, not elected.

classes.name: Alcaldías y vicealcaldías
classes.finest_note: Votes by administrative and electoral district in the Cómputo de votos books and workbooks
classes.note: Each canton elects a mayor by relative majority (Código Electoral art. 202), with two alternates in 2002 and 2006 and a first and second vice-mayor since 2010 (Código Municipal art. 14). The Código Municipal of 1998 replaced the council-appointed ejecutivo municipal; the first direct election was in December 2002, separate from the national elections, and since February 2016 all municipal posts are elected together two years after the national elections. Mayors may be removed by plebiscite (class consulta_cantonal).

cadence.vacancy_rule: The first vice-mayor, then the second, completes the term; if both are removed or resign, the TSE calls an election in the canton within six months (Código Municipal art. 19; Código Electoral art. 147).

classes.name: Regidurías del concejo municipal
classes.finest_note: Votes by administrative and electoral district in the Cómputo de votos books and workbooks from 2002; the 1998 declarations give cantons
classes.note: Each canton's council of regidores, five to thirteen by population (Código Municipal art. 21; Constitution art. 171), elected by closed lists in the canton by cociente and subcociente (Código Electoral arts. 201-205). Elected with the national elections until February 2010 and with the municipal elections since February 2016 (the 2010 councils served six years). Municipal councils go back to the nineteenth century; the TSE's published declarations begin in 1998.

cadence.vacancy_rule: Filled by the next candidate on the party's cantonal list (Código Electoral art. 208); the TSE calls a partial election only if the council disintegrates (art. 147).

classes.name: Plebiscitos, referendos y cabildos municipales
classes.note: A municipal council may call plebiscites, referendos and cabildos under a regulation drafted with the TSE, whose delegates attend (Código Municipal art. 13(k)), and must call a plebiscite on removing the mayor when three quarters of the regidores approve a motion; removal needs two thirds of votes cast and at least 10 percent of the canton's electors (art. 19).
classes.disposition_reason: Each municipality runs and records its own consultations; the TSE publishes no list or results of them.

classes.name: Sindicaturas
classes.finest_note: Votes by administrative and electoral district in the Cómputo de votos books and workbooks from 2002
classes.note: Each district elects a síndico and an alternate by relative majority (Código Electoral art. 202); the síndico sits on the municipal council with voice but no vote (Constitution art. 172) and chairs the district council or the concejo municipal de distrito. Elected with the national elections until 1998, in December 2002, 2006 and 2010, and with the other municipal posts since 2016.

cadence.vacancy_rule: The alternate síndico completes the term.

classes.name: Intendencias y viceintendencias
classes.finest_note: Votes by administrative and electoral district in the Cómputo de votos books and workbooks
classes.note: Each concejo municipal de distrito (Ley General de Concejos Municipales de Distrito, Law 8173 of 2002) elects an intendente, its executive, by relative majority, with a vice-intendente since 2010. Eight districts had one from 2002 to 2020; Monteverde became a canton in 2022, leaving seven.
